speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I need to investigate the causes of your jaundice, itching, weight loss, and changes in stool and urine color. To start, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any abdominal pain or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 72-year-old male. The patient has experienced gradual yellow discoloration of the skin and generalized pruritus over the past 2 weeks. He also reports a decreased appetite and a weight loss of 6.3 kg (14 lb). The patient’s stool has been pale, and his urine is very dark. Three years ago, he had an episode of acute upper abdominal pain, which was managed with IV fluids, NSAIDs, and dietary modification. The patient has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 year...

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Given your age and the combination of painless jaundice, significant weight loss, pale stools, and dark urine, I am concerned about an obstruction in the bile duct. You mentioned a history of abdominal pain three years ago; was that pain located in the upper right side or epigastrium?

REQUEST TEST: Liver Function Panel, CA 19-9, CEA
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Choledocholithiasis or malignancy causing Extrahepatic Biliary Obstruction (suggested by the cystic mass and biliary dilation). Given your age, weight loss, and painless jaundice with an anechoic cystic mass in the subhepatic region, we must strongly suspect a cholangiocarcinoma or a large impacted stone. I will need a CT of the abdomen with contrast or an MRCP to better characterize this mass before we proceed with treatment.
